author: Crabtaculous
quote: Visually appealing repetitive combat that takes no intuition whatsoever.  The graphics are good, but the character designs are atrocious. Wolverine looks soft and cherubic.... meh. Wolverine should have a menacing grimace of a man trying to pass a massive lead bolus.  What else, oh Lady Psylockestrike what were they thinking when they created that hideous abomination. Everything is wrong about this game, I gave it a three because for a brief time you can squint and pretend your playing a cool Wolverine game..

author: Crabtaculous
quote: A stuttering mess of an already handicapped framerate of 30 FPS. It feels like you're moving through molasses as the frames dip from 24 to 17. That said the graphics are appealing and the world is well designed but over purposed. The game runs best when you're doing mundane boring life simulator missions. Looks great, but we didn't pay $80 to $100 dollars to do boring chores and shopping. Everything has been given a process, pointless quick times to create a pseudo immersion.  No longer do you press Y to perform the games namesake, and your player character figures it out being a criminal and all. No, no you have to perform arbitrary button presses and joystick motions to choose the handle, smash the window, slim Jim, then another arbitrary double stick work to hot wire the car. Even after all this trash mechanics, you have to go through hoops to keep the vehicle. Shopping is tedious, eating is tedious, too much put into pointless activities.  On to the story, so far the story mediocre, the first time in GTA's history you play a character with no agency. An enormous beautiful open world playing a character with no freedom.  I see the big picture in the games design is you're pigeonholed into playing missions and sticking to the story. Causing havoc and having fun like the GTA of old is too much work, in the name of "realism'.  Losing wanted level now takes multiple finite steps that end up discouraging exploration and doing the things that put this franchise on the map.  Final verdict, a boring overhyped stuttering festival of glitches. That is absolutely unacceptable for a company that has been making GTA sandbox games since 2001, and invested two billion in creating this slop.

author: Crabtaculous
quote:
Excellent story, and writing set in a beautifully recreated nook of the Gothic Era Carpathian Range. The graphics are exceptional, with sublime looking environments, and fairly realistic textures. The denizens of this world  look as if they live a hard life, and game's aesthetic is very refreshing in the current climate of entertainment.  The combat takes a bit to master, but once you do it is very rewarding, and visually captivating. Which is a good thing, because there is a lot of fighting. The animation is smooth and well done by open world sandbox standards, and the dialog is exceptional. 

My gripes are few, and I will keep them spoiler free. An additional way to get around the world would of been nice. If your not a fan either of the two expedited travel options you're stuck legging it across the countryside.  There is also an aspect of the story I wish you could stop. 

Other than that, Blood of the Dawnwalker is a refreshing game unhindered by the trapping of current times which really creates an immersive experience.  I highly recommend  it for its fantastic, gameplay, open ended objective structure, beautifully rendered graphics and animation.
